chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about one who deliberately kills a believer, is there for him repentance? He said: 'He does not receive forgiveness until he pays his blood money (diyah) to his family, frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, seeks forgiveness of Allah, repents to Him, and supplicates humbly; for indeed I hope that forgiveness will be granted to him if he does that.' I said: 'And if he has no wealth to pay his blood money?' He said: 'He asks the Muslims until he pays his blood money to his family.'

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing
key_terms.رَقَبَة: Slave or captive, specifically for manumission

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for repentance after deliberately killing a believer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the multifaceted expiation (kaffarah) for deliberate homicide, emphasizing that spiritual repentance is inextricably linked to the material restitution of blood money (diyah) to the victim's heirs. Notably, it highlights the communal responsibility in Shia jurisprudence, as the killer may solicit funds from the Muslim community if he lacks personal wealth, ensuring the debt is cleared before seeking divine forgiveness.
